movies.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death in the Outback
movies.blurb: A gripping, cinematic documentary series that reconstructs one of Australia’s defining contemporary events, exposing the enduring legacies of race, justice, and colonial policing.

movies.title: A Common Story
movies.blurb: Starring Alba Rohrwacher (Three Goodbyes, TIFF ’25) and Guido Caprino, writer-director Anna Foglietta’s heartfelt debut feature follows nascent empty nesters who encounter old desires while seeking new meaning in their lives.

movies.title: A Girl Unknown
movies.blurb: In Zou Jing’s assured debut, Cao Ruofan and Li Gengxi (Bi Gan’s Resurrection) portray a girl passed through three different families and identities under China’s one-child policy. Visually refined, this affecting coming-of-age drama explores resilience and self-determination.

movies.title: A Good Little Soldier
movies.blurb: In Stéphane Brizé’s latest capitalist critique, Carla (Alba Rohrwacher) is pushed to her moral limits when she is recruited to rebrand a company’s image, compromising people for profit to serve her corporate supervisors.

movies.title: A Long Winter
movies.blurb: After his mother disappears during the first blizzard of the season, a young man refuses to give up hope as one long Montana winter reshapes his relationship with his father and his understanding of the man he is becoming. From Andrew Haigh, the acclaimed director of All of Us Strangers.

movies.title: A Talent for Murder
movies.blurb: This smouldering chamber thriller from Anton Corbijn (Control) stars Oscar winner Helen Mirren and Alden Ehrenreich (Fair Play) as opponents in a strange confrontation between a youthful literary agent and The Talented Mr. Ripley author Patricia Highsmith.

movies.title: After Elena
movies.blurb: When a family's matriarch dies, four relatives are forced to confront decades of silence, resentment, and buried affection. Led by Alfredo Castro, this sharp ensemble balances humour and melancholy in a moving portrait of grief and reconciliation.

movies.title: Ah Girl
movies.blurb: Winner of the Youth Jury Award at the 55th International Film Festival Rotterdam, Ang Geck Geck Priscilla’s feature debut is a bittersweet yet heartwarming story of a young girl as she tries to figure out what it means to become an adult.

movies.title: Alice
movies.blurb: Amidst the advent of modern cinema, trailblazing artist Alice Guy becomes the first female film director in this lush historical series starring Academy Award–nominee Bérénice Bejo (The Artist).

movies.title: All About Corinne
movies.blurb: Paris Follies writer-director Marc Fitoussi re-teams with the inimitable, Oscar-nominated Isabelle Huppert (TIFF ’16’s Elle) for this delectable comedy about a veteran background actor who spies a belated chance to break into the fickle family of le cinéma français.

movies.title: All of a Sudden
movies.blurb: Ryûsuke Hamaguchi brings Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto together in a poignant drama about friendship, illness, art, and the responsibilities of care, creating a film that makes the world seem gentler, more open, and more humane.

movies.title: All That She Wants
movies.blurb: Annie Murphy (Schitt’s Creek) stars in this effervescent, tender-hearted, refreshingly modern rom-com that chronicles a casual encounter between a millennial and a Gen Zer — and the life-altering consequences that result.

movies.title: Alpha Gang
movies.blurb: Léa Seydoux, Dave Bautista, Lily-Rose Depp, and Cate Blanchett star in the Zellner brothers’ look at an alien gang coming to Earth to conquer, but finding the human world has a plague they weren’t ready for.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre
VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Always Lalisa
movies.blurb: K-pop idol–turned–global superstar Lisa stars in this intimate and transformative documentary tracing her journey from childhood ambition through BLACKPINK stardom into the artist she is today.

movies.title: American Hostage
movies.blurb: Jon Hamm stars in this adaptation of the hit podcast, which tells the true story of an Indianapolis radio reporter thrust into a high-stakes situation when a local man takes a bank employee hostage and demands to be interviewed live on air.

movies.title: Ancestors
movies.blurb: A haunting journey set in 1980s London, David Turpin’s mesmerizing debut transforms one young man’s search for a missing friend into an unforgettable story of love, loss, and gay legacy.

movies.title: Anchors Aweigh
movies.blurb: After a thwarted marriage proposal, alt-comedian Matt Barats spirals into an existential crisis in this semi-autobiographical blend of deadpan absurdism and unexpected poignancy told in a first-person, confessional style à la Ross McElwee or John Wilson.

movies.title: Angh
movies.blurb: In a deserted Nagaland village in the early 1960s, a chief must choose between his family and a transforming world embodied by an incoming American missionary in filmmaker Theja Rio’s gripping feature-length adaptation of his award-winning 2021 short.

movies.title: Arne Goes to Space
movies.blurb: An extraterrestrial visitor upends the lives of two elderly brothers in northern Sweden in Lars Vega’s disarming blend of sci-fi fable and small-town comedy.

movies.title: Arrested Memory
movies.blurb: A seasoned detective (Ethan Juan) recently diagnosed with dementia is doggedly pursued by both cops and crooks after he unwittingly wanders off with a multimillion-dollar ransom in a new absurdist crime caper from cult auteur SABU.

movies.title: Ashes
movies.blurb: Diego Luna crafts a powerful and deeply humane portrait of the immigrant experience through the eyes of a young woman forced to rebuild her life in a new country, delivering a nuanced exploration of family, identity, belonging, and displacement.

movies.title: At Night
movies.blurb: Mesmerizing and melancholic, the much-anticipated debut feature by British filmmaker and artist Beatrice Gibson is a work of choral autofiction that shifts from narrative to documentary to dream over a single night in Paris, reflecting on the nature of womanhood, privilege, and solidarity.

movies.title: Atonement
movies.blurb: Boyd Holbrook (The Bikeriders), Hiam Abbass (TIFF ’25’s Palestine 36), and Oscar winner Kenneth Branagh star in Oscar-nominated writer-director Reed Van Dyk’s searing story of trauma and forgiveness following a horrifying event during the Iraq War.

movies.title: Ba's Book
movies.blurb: In a hybrid documentary retelling, documentary filmmaker Ashley Duong takes her father’s memoir and stages a recreation of it in Vietnam alongside her family.

movies.title: Babies
movies.blurb: Seth Rogen and Oscar nominee Anna Kendrick (TIFF ’09’s Up in the Air) star in Lauren Miller Rogen’s big-hearted comedy about the dilemma that eventually infiltrates every long-term relationship: to parent or not to parent?

movies.title: Back in Black
movies.blurb: Christopher Walken leads a terrific cast in director Ron Murphy’s hilarious satire about a failing family funeral home that experiences a reversal of fortune thanks to their town’s suspicious spike in fatality rates.

movies.title: Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo
movies.blurb: The latest from prolific maestro Takashi Miike, like Abel Ferrara’s Bad Lieutenant (TIFF ’92) and Werner Herzog’s Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call — New Orleans (TIFF ’09), is a sensational ride through the darkest crevasses of the criminal underworld.

movies.title: Bedford Park
movies.blurb: Writer-director Stephanie Ahn’s feature debut explores the complexities of diasporic experience through a chance encounter between two thirtysomething, second-generation Korean Americans, tracking their relationship as it moves from circumstantial to friendly to romantic.

movies.title: Being Heumann
movies.blurb: Featuring a breakout performance by Ruth Madeley and Oscar nominee Mark Ruffalo (TIFF ’15’s Spotlight), this inspiring historical drama from Oscar-winning filmmaker Siân Heder (CODA) celebrates the paradigm-shifting activist Judy Heumann, “Mother of the Disability Rights Movement.”

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre
VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Below
movies.blurb: Something monstrous lurks off the coast in this suspenseful, Newfoundland-set limited series, starring Josh Hartnett (Trap) and Mackenzie Davis (Station Eleven).

movies.title: Ben'Imana
movies.blurb: In this powerful, feminist debut feature, which won the Caméra d’Or at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo brilliantly explores the issue of forgiveness in the wake of the Tutsi genocide in Rwanda.

movies.title: Bitter Christmas
movies.blurb: With noirish hues and telenovela twists, the latest from Oscar-winning maestro Pedro Almodóvar (TIFF ’24’s The Room Next Door) follows a pair of self-centred film directors exploring grief, love, and the perils of unchecked artistic license.

movies.title: Black Sunflowers
movies.blurb: Black Sunflowers is a mosaic of Ukrainian youth, shuttling between the frontlines and civilian life, captured by the gifted American filmmaker James Marcus Haney (No Cameras Allowed) collaborating with an esteemed Ukrainian crew.

movies.title: Bleeding Hearts
movies.blurb: This real-life love story follows the charismatic musicians Zella Day and Jesse Woods as they team to create the alt-country band Chaparelle with collaborator Beau Bedford, in a documentary with as much drama as a season of Nashville.

movies.title: Blindspot Berlin
movies.blurb: This gripping thriller depicts the investigation — and its shortfalls — in the months before the December 2016 attack at the Christmas market at Breitscheidplatz, Berlin.

movies.title: Brace Your Heart
movies.blurb: Amanda Kernell’s luminous third drama is a richly observed portrait of love, resilience, and the enduring strength of Sámi women in northernmost Europe.

movies.title: Bucking Fastard
movies.blurb: Director Werner Herzog and real-life sisters Kate and Rooney Mara enliven the wild true story of twin sisters who speak as one, fall in love with the same person, and eventually spiral in a peculiar case that grabbed national headlines in 1980s Britain.

movies.title: Bunker
movies.blurb: Oscar winners Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem play a couple whose bond is tested when a mysterious billionaire’s proposal prompts an ethical impasse in the latest from Oscar-winning writer-director Florian Zeller (TIFF ’20’s The Father).

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Carrie
movies.blurb: Vanguard of character-driven horror Mike Flanagan (Life of Chuck, TIFF ’24) returns to episodic storytelling with this kinetic adaptation of Stephen King’s classic novel, about the cruelty faced by a sheltered young girl entering high school.

movies.title: Cheyenne
movies.blurb: Cheyenne follows a group of fearless cowgirls who compete at riding wild broncos on the rodeo circuit after nearly a century of being excluded because of their gender.

movies.title: Children Untold
movies.blurb: Acclaimed filmmaker and author Miwa Nishikawa adapts her forthcoming novel into a compassionate and clear-eyed postwar drama about a 12-year-old orphan who disguises herself as a boy, featuring a striking performance by newcomer Ami Koyae and a memorable supporting turn by Koji Yakusho.

movies.title: Clarissa
movies.blurb: Led by a stellar cast including Sophie Okonedo and David Oyelowo, filmmaking brothers Arie and Chuko Esiri’s second feature is a beguiling adaptation of Virginia Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway set in contemporary Lagos.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Closing Night
movies.blurb: Naomi Watts, Sarah Paulson, and Odessa A’zion deliver powerhouse performances in Cody Fern’s sensational feature debut, where a hardened movie star reunites with the deliciously messy family she left behind decades earlier.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Club Kid
movies.blurb: In his exuberant debut feature, writer-director Jordan Firstman stars as a carousing New York City club promoter whose lifestyle is upended by the unexpected responsibility of raising a 10-year-old son he never knew he had.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Congo Boy
movies.blurb: Drawing upon director Rafiki Fariala’s own experience as a displaced Congolese finding purpose in art, this rousing character study follows a young man trying to care for his family while forging his own path as a rapper in Bangui.

movies.title: Conversation With The Sea
movies.blurb: Condemned to pay the social security contributions owed by his son, a father (Kamel El Basha) desperately tries to prove his death in the moving drama Conversation With The Sea.

movies.title: Coward
movies.blurb: Belgian director Lukas Dhont’s poignant third feature celebrates a love that blooms amid the hardships and horrors of the First World War.

movies.title: Crystal Lake
movies.blurb: Set long before the events of Friday the 13th, Linda Cardellini stars as Pamela Voorhees in this captivating, A24-produced origin series.

movies.title: Darlene Love: I Know Where I've Been
movies.blurb: Stars like Bruce Springsteen, Cher, and Dionne Warwick sing the praises of an underappreciated musical icon in this high-spirited and warm-hearted portrait from Canadian director Barry Avrich (Oscar Peterson: Black + White, TIFF ’21).

movies.title: Diary of a Mad Old Man
movies.blurb: This captivating adaptation of Jun’ichirō Tanizaki’s novel from director Wayne Wang (TIFF ’93’s The Joy Luck Club) follows an aging widower drawn into an unnervingly intimate relationship with his caregiver daughter-in-law.

movies.title: Djinn Wedding
movies.blurb: Set in a remote Anatolian village, Ferit Karahan’s Djinn Wedding is an impressive family drama that unravels family secrets and conflicts across three periods of time.

movies.title: Dorothy
movies.blurb: Set in a world shaped by caste, violence, and toxic masculinity, two childhood friends grow up inseparable in rural Tamil Nadu. Their lives are transformed by the arrival of Dorothy, a woman whose compassion quietly challenges the world around them.

movies.title: Double Freedom
movies.blurb: Less follow-up or sequel to his breakout debut than a sly and clever echo, Lisandro Alonso’s graceful and extraordinarily beautiful Double Freedom returns us to the daily life of Misael, a solitary labourer in Argentina’s rural La Pampa.

movies.title: Drifter
movies.blurb: Fast & Furious alum Sung Kang directs and stars in this alternately melancholy and exhilarating character study of a lonesome racetrack custodian with a secret talent for drifting.

movies.title: Edward Said: Between Worlds
movies.blurb: Palestinian scholar Edward Said is profiled in his own words, drawing upon decades of archives, to explore the legacy of his groundbreaking works including Orientalism and The Question of Palestine.

movies.title: Eklipse
movies.blurb: As the highly anticipated 1999 solar eclipse comes and goes, everything that was shrouded in darkness suddenly comes to light in Eklipse, the feature-length debut of Austrian writer-director Manuel Wetscher, whose penchant for poetic realism brings emotional turbulence to a bucolic setting.

movies.title: Elephants in the Fog
movies.blurb: A village matriarch (Puspa Thing Lama) must choose between her heart’s desires and her duty to her community when a young woman disappears into the forest in this delicate, riveting thriller.

movies.title: Elsinore
movies.blurb: Andrew Scott (TIFF ’25’s Blue Moon and Wake Up Dead Man) delivers his strongest performance honouring the real-life story of Ian Charleson, the Chariots of Fire actor who courageously pushed through AIDS to play Hamlet at London’s National Theatre.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Everest: The Other Side
movies.blurb: Professional ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson seek to ski down the North Face of Mount Everest, a feat never achieved, as the Oscar-winning filmmakers Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin (Free Solo, TIFF ’18) follow their journey, shooting for the IMAX screen.

movies.title: Everybody Wants to F*ck Me
movies.blurb: Taron Egerton gives a gleefully committed performance as a man determined to be viewed by potential paramours as the ideal catch in director Jonathan Schey’s darkly comic appraisal of modern dating and how some men signal virtues they don’t possess.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Everything Else is Noise
movies.blurb: Prolific Mexican-Canadian auteur Nicolás Pereda has delivered his sharpest and most amusing film yet with Everything Else is Noise, a sly, self-reflexive comedy of manners and mishaps involving a trio of women classical composers and musicians.

movies.title: Everytime
movies.blurb: A grieving mother and her late daughter’s boyfriend explore questions of guilt, grief, and forgiveness on a family holiday, in Sandra Wollner’s bold and haunting Un Certain Regard winner.

movies.title: Evil Genius
movies.blurb: Featuring David Harbour (Stranger Things) and Oscar winner Patricia Arquette (Boyhood), Courteney Cox’s second feature as director boldly dramatizes the chilling, darkly hilarious web of stories behind 2003’s infamous “pizza bomber” incident.

movies.title: Faith
movies.blurb: The spark of romance offers a hard-working single mother (Erin Doherty, The Crown) the chance to imagine a different future. But after tragedy strikes, she discovers that the man she may be falling for (James McAvoy) is hiding a truth she couldn’t have imagined.

movies.title: Fjord
movies.blurb: Winner of the prestigious Palme d’Or at this year’s Cannes Film Festival, the latest from writer-director Cristian Mungiu is a gripping high-stakes courtroom drama driven by a profound moral dilemma.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Flies
movies.blurb: When a lonely woman rents a room to a father with a hospitalized relative, she forms an unexpected bond with his young son, in Fernando Eimbcke’s tender story about care, connection, and quiet transformation.

movies.title: Four Seasons in Java
movies.blurb: Kamila Andini, the brilliant mind behind TIFF ’21 Platform Award winner Yuni, returns with another polished and picturesque film with a strong women's narrative, starring Indonesia’s biggest talents Putri Marino, Christine Hakim, and Arya Saloka.

movies.title: Furies
movies.blurb: Set in a bankrupt and sweaty Beirut, Rami Kodeih’s impressive thriller follows two sisters in need of money for an important surgery.

movies.title: Future Tense
movies.blurb: With Future Tense, Jenna Cato Bass deals with climate change, human guilt, and South Africa’s identity in this bold time-lapse story based in the near future.

movies.title: Gail
movies.blurb: This music documentary on an Our Lady Peace superfan follows her on the band’s 30th anniversary Canadian tour, and boasts an original score by Lesley Barber (Bonjour Tristesse, TIFF ’24), and orchestral arrangements by Eric Rosse (Tori Amos’ Little Earthquakes).

movies.title: Gentle Monster
movies.blurb: Featuring emotional performances from Léa Seydoux (TIFF ’25’s Silent Friend) and Jella Haase, writer-director Marie Kreutzer’s follow-up to TIFF ’22’s Corsage is a dual portrait of women trapped in moral maelstroms caused by men’s malfeasance.

movies.title: Girl Group
movies.blurb: Rebel Wilson writes, directs, and stars in this story of a pop star who, following a downward spiral, finds a new sense of purpose by assembling a bunch of young up-and-comers to form a group of their own.

movies.title: Glaxo
movies.blurb: Glaxo, Benjamín Naishtat’s riveting adaptation of Hernán Ronsino’s novel, transforms a single betrayal into an absorbing tale of guilt, loyalty, and memory, weaving personal tragedy with Argentina’s turbulent twentieth-century history through an atmosphere of mounting mystery and suspense.

movies.title: God Bless You, Mr Kopu
movies.blurb: A charismatic salesman promises wealth, success, and a fresh start — but at what cost? Alex Liu's wildly entertaining debut blends dark comedy, social satire, and a propulsive thriller into a sharp exploration of ambition and identity.

movies.title: Growth of the Soil
movies.blurb: Nobel Prize-winner Knut Hamsun’s novel about a farmer’s struggles in early 20th-century Norway gets a powerful and richly textured adaptation by director Hans Petter Moland and his superb cast.

movies.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
movies.blurb: Oscar nominee Rinko Kikuchi (TIFF ’06’s Babel) stars in this fantasy-fuelled fable from director Josef Kubota Wladyka (Catch the Fair One), which follows a Tokyo ballroom enthusiast as she dreams and dances her way through spells of bliss and sorrow.

movies.title: HALF
movies.blurb: Twin half-blooded vampires (Ranjith Sajeev and Aiswarya Raj) wage war with desert highway hijackers in a gory martial arts curry western from writer-director Samjad and choreographer Very Tri Yulisman (The Raid 2, The Night Comes for Us).

movies.title: Happily Ever After
movies.blurb: American Girl director Feng-I Fiona Roan’s sophomore film explores the definition of happiness through the lens of two sisters, backed by breakout performances from Xuan Chen and singer-turned-actress Shu-hua Yeh of i-dle.

movies.title: Head to Head
movies.blurb: Iranian filmmaker Ghasideh Golmakani’s absurd and sharply satirical debut feature explores what happens when a female director forces male actors to wear skirts and headscarves.

movies.title: Hombre al agua
movies.blurb: The latest directorial feature from Gael García Bernal (TIFF ’19’s Chicuarotes) is a psychologically astute comedy of manners for the modern age, following an ensemble of eclectic characters seeking to become something more than who they are.

movies.title: Hope
movies.blurb: In this madcap marvel from Na Hong-jin (The Chaser, The Wailing), a police chief (Hwang Jung-min) and deputy (Hoyeon) investigate a monstrous incursion upon their remote village, as a headstrong local (Zo In-sung) musters a hunting party to root out the threat.

movies.title: How We Stand
movies.blurb: How We Stand combines magical realism, a story of sisters separated by tragedy, and a cast of rising Indigenous talent. Starring Amber Midthunder, Alyssa Wapanatâhk, Isabel DeRoy-Olson, and Cara Jade Myers.

movies.title: I Am Mario
movies.blurb: A transgender taxi driver’s dream of fatherhood becomes a reality when he gets pregnant, forcing him to confront his own notions of masculinity while navigating unexpected social, moral, and emotional consequences.

movies.title: I Play Rocky
movies.blurb: Featuring a career-making performance from Anthony Ippolito, the latest from Oscar winner Peter Farrelly (TIFF ’18 People’s Choice Award winner Green Book) vividly recreates the story of how an unknown named Sylvester Stallone got Rocky produced — and became a superstar.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre
VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Idda
movies.blurb: When two childhood friends meet after years to fulfill the broken promise of climbing Mount Etna, Adele and Sofia realize that like the mountain, old wounds loom over everything.

movies.title: In Alaska
movies.blurb: When a suicidal Inuk teen accidentally pierces an oil pipeline with a bullet, the FBI launches a full-scale manhunt across the northern wilderness in this drama starring Noomi Rapace (The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo) and newcomer Leo Matthew Temela.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: In the Heart of the South
movies.blurb: In the Heart of the South is what Single White Female would be if it were set in Toronto, with an Inuk protagonist and a dash of supernatural elements, starring North of North’s Anna Lambe.

movies.title: In Waves
movies.blurb: Set under the confectionery pink and blue skies of California, this animated film narrates the love story between a young skater and a surfer who share a mutual passion for the ocean.

movies.title: Inherit
movies.blurb: Davika Hoorne plays her most magnetic role yet as Woranart – a grandma possessed by a demon – in the latest chilling psychological thriller by Shutter director Banjong Pisanthanakun.

movies.title: Ink
movies.blurb: Director Danny Boyle’s latest thrillingly charts the meteoric rise of Rupert Murdoch’s fledgling but instantly notorious The Sun newspaper as he and editor Larry Lamb create the blueprint for UK tabloid culture. Guy Pearce (The Brutalist, TIFF ’24) and Jack O’Connell star.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Intermission
movies.blurb: Yonfan transforms excerpts from his 15 films into a brilliant, genre-defying meditation on cinema, memory, beauty, desire, and his own singular body of work, featuring Maggie Cheung, Chow Yun-fat, Sylvia Chang, Shu Qi, Daniel Wu, and many, many more.

movies.title: Iron Boy
movies.blurb: Winner of the Special Jury Prize at Cannes last spring, Pixar animator Louis Clichy’s gorgeous hand-painted animation tells the story of a boy in need of a back brace who seeks the courage to stand alone.

movies.title: It Will Happen Tonight
movies.blurb: Louis Garrel (TIFF ’25’s Couture) leads a charming ensemble in this decades-spanning divine dramady from Nanni Moretti (TIFF ’01’s The Son’s Room) that will restore your faith in destiny and the wild logic of the heart.

movies.title: It's My Time
movies.blurb: Led by Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh (Everything Everywhere All at Once), this inspired comedy about a woman on the road to magic-cube mastery is a story of galvanizing gamesmanship and ageless defiance.

movies.title: Josephine
movies.blurb: After witnessing a sexual assault, a young girl is haunted by the trauma of the disturbing incident, opening her eyes to the violence that surrounds her.

movies.title: Julián
movies.blurb: From the acclaimed studio behind Wolfwalkers and Song of the Sea comes a joyful adaptation of Jessica Love’s beloved children’s book about a young boy whose dream of becoming a mermaid transforms both his summer and his relationship with his grandmother.

movies.title: Ken Russell's The Devils
movies.blurb: North American Premiere of 4K restoration!

movies.title: Kick On
movies.blurb: Looking to prolong their night of partying, four youths are plunged into paranoid pandemonium after crossing a mobster’s volatile son in Nick Kozakis’ bloody ripper of a siege thriller.

movies.title: Kissed
movies.blurb:
World Premiere of 4K restoration!

 Initially a controversial outlier, Lynne Stopkewich’s singular debut Kissed (TIFF ’96) is a subversive, tender drama about sexual awakening that shares the same ethereal atmosphere as erotic Canadian classics David Cronenberg’s Crash (1996) and Atom Egoyan’s Exotica (1994).

movies.title: Krux
movies.blurb: The feature debut of writer-director Tony Vahl delivers a powerful and stark portrait of moral collapse, societal panic, and the consequences of being on the wrong side of history.

movies.title: L'AUTRE
movies.blurb: Wild delusions and genuine dangers threaten a patient recovering from cancer surgery in this visceral and darkly comedic thriller by Quebec’s Alexandre Franchi.

movies.title: La Bola Negra
movies.blurb: Los Javis’ ambitious and captivating homage to Federico García Lorca sees the lives of three men intertwined in love and loss across eras. Featuring powerful performances by Guitarricadelafuente, Carlos González, and Miguel Bernardeau.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre
VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: La Gradiva
movies.blurb: A pack of rowdy French teenagers embark on a school field trip to Pompeii, where desire, passion, angst, and class tensions in the present unfold against the ruins of the ancient past.

movies.title: Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney
movies.blurb: This kaleidoscopic culture jam from visionary filmmaker Matthew Rankin (The Twentieth Century, Universal Language) details the rise of Canada’s 18th prime minister through a satirical collage of archival footage, television nostalgia, and national mythmaking.

movies.title: Le Faux Soir
movies.blurb: Inspired by a fact-based act of subversive irreverence in Nazi-occupied Brussels, Michaël R. Roskam’s thriller delivers a historical drama that feels more like a heist movie.

movies.title: Lemonade
movies.blurb: Lewis Brophy delivers a breakout performance in Kim Bartley’s compassionate debut drama about Irish teen, forced to leave foster care on his 18th birthday, who must find his way in a world that suddenly expects him to be a man.

movies.title: Life of Jorge Luis Borges
movies.blurb: With the erudition and insight of a literary scholar and the gumption of an amateur detective, Argentinian auteur (and raconteur) Mariano Llinás (La Flor, TIFF ’18) explores the life and fiction of the legendary writer Jorge Luis Borges through objects and places.

movies.title: Light Pillar
movies.blurb: A lonely caretaker, a dying film studio, and a seductive virtual world collide in Xu Zao’s formally daring animated debut feature: a melancholic, visionary parable about cinema, technology, alienation, and the fragile promise of renewal.

movies.title: Like Magic
movies.blurb: Blending archival footage, personal testimony, and a decades-long search for answers, Melissa Saavedra Gil transforms a childhood tragedy into a powerful exploration of memory, truth, and healing. An intimate and deeply resonant debut that illuminates both a personal story and a generation shaped by violence.

movies.title: London
movies.blurb: An experimental yet tender road movie about an enigmatic man’s shared commutes across Austria’s scenic West Autobahn — shot in-studio with vintage rear-projection techniques — Sebastian Brameshuber’s award-winning London is a rare work of technical prowess that never belies its emotional core.

movies.title: Long Long Night
movies.blurb: This deeply moving debut from Kyu Bock Youm is a radiantly detailed animation chronicling the peripatetic lives of a rhino and a penguin as they traverse a vast, ever-changing wilderness brimming with natural beauty and human-generated danger.

movies.title: Look Back
movies.blurb: Visionary auteur Hirokazu Kore-eda helms this tender and slow-burning adaptation of manga creator Tatsuki Fujimoto’s acclaimed story, following two young artists whose friendship and bond become the engine of their art.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Love is the monster
movies.blurb: In a chilling dystopian thriller shaped by fear and inequality, Neto Villalobos Brenes follows a grandmother, powerfully portrayed by Paulina García, whose granddaughter's kidnapping forces her into impossible moral choices.

movies.title: Love of Your Life
movies.blurb: Featuring a beautifully understated performance from Margaret Qualley (TIFF ’24’s The Substance), this sweeping romantic character study from director Rachel Morrison (TIFF ’24’s The Fire Inside) is an exhilarating testament to loving fully, making amends, and moving on.

movies.title: Low Lies The Land
movies.blurb: Set in the breathtaking landscapes of Piemonte in Northern Italy, Low Lies the Land immerses us in the lives of three winemaking families facing an uncertain future.

movies.title: Magazine
movies.blurb: Set in New York’s cliquish literary scene, writer-director Alexandra Pechman’s feature debut chronicles the sentimental education of an aspiring poet (Lily McInerny, TIFF ’24’s Bonjour Tristesse) who becomes tangled in a web of eros, cultural gatekeeping, and office intrigue.

movies.title: Man in Motion: The Rick Hansen Story
movies.blurb: This galvanizing portrait celebrates Rick Hansen, the great Canadian athlete and activist. It chronicles his 26-month Man In Motion World Tour: a 40,000-kilometre wheelchair journey that raised millions to eliminate accessibility barriers and transform public perception of people with disabilities.

movies.title: Marie Madeleine
movies.blurb: Géssica Généus directs and stars in this vibrant reimagining of the biblical tale of Mary Magdalene, following a free-spirited Haitian sex worker whose serendipitous involvement with a repressed preacher’s son opens each to possibilities.

movies.title: Masc
movies.blurb: This debut feature from London-based artist Bertil Nilsson is a tender, unflinching portrait of self-performance, identity, and the quiet but persistent work of learning to exist as oneself in an often prescriptive world.

movies.title: Memories of a Forest
movies.blurb: Katharina Rabl’s stunning debut feature toggles between loyalty and longing for independence, centring a doctoral student who must choose between carrying on her family’s legacy or forging her own path.

movies.title: Minotaur
movies.blurb: After a nine-year hiatus, during which he fled his native Russia into exile, Andrey Zvyagintsev (The Return, TIFF ’03, Leviathan, TIFF ’14) returns with a reworking of Claude Chabrol's La femme infidèle, adapted to his homeland's current rhetoric of patriarchy and warmongering.

movies.title: Misty Green
movies.blurb: Featuring a career-making performance from Slow Horses’ Rosalind Eleazar and supporting turns from Daniel Kaluuya, Adam Driver, and Anna Kendrick, Chris Rock’s latest as writer-director brilliantly satirizes the bigotry and hustle at the heart of Hollywood.

movies.title: Mr. Nelson, Did You Kill People?
movies.blurb: Cult Japanese filmmaker Shinya Tsukamoto directs acclaimed Broadway actor Rodney Hicks and Oscar winner Geoffrey Rush in a harrowing, visceral, and morally urgent portrait of Vietnam veteran Allen Nelson.

movies.title: Musk
movies.blurb: The Oscar-winning documentarian Alex Gibney delivers his most ambitious and epic work in exploring the history of the world’s richest man, Elon Musk.

movies.title: Muyi
movies.blurb: A teenager undertakes a fantastic journey in order to save her mountaintop village where men are forbidden, in Julien Chheng’s charming and magical animated feature.

movies.title: My Wife Cries
movies.blurb: With My Wife Cries — a startling, minimalist study in romantic misalignment — German auteur and Festival favourite Angela Schanelec employs her singular style to portray the crushing anguish and vertiginous confusion brought forth by marital crisis.

movies.title: Neil Peart: No One's Disciple
movies.blurb: Geddy Lee and Alex Lifeson team up with four revered drummers — Stewart Copeland, Danny Carey, Chad Smith, and Gavin Harrison — for an exhilarating and poignant tribute to late Rush legend Neil Peart.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Neverman
movies.blurb: Broadway and cabaret icon Justin Vivian Bond stars as a transgender gay rights activist with worsening Alzheimer disease suffering from the treatment in her nursing home, in Rodrigo Barriuso’s poignant second feature.

movies.title: Nobody's Violence
movies.blurb: Larissa Corriveau delivers a striking performance as an enigmatic death-dealer in this bold, bracing, and Buñuelian feature by Denis Côté.

movies.title: Nosotros
movies.blurb: After leaving his Indigenous family for work in Guatemala City, a lonely security guard falls for a business owner at the mall he patrols, discovering an unexpected refuge and a new sense of self in a world not yet ready to make space for them.

movies.title: Obsession
movies.blurb: When a hopeless romantic makes a wish that his long-time crush falls in love with him, a sinister enchantment ensues in writer-director Curry Barker’s freaky and frightening feature debut.

movies.title: On Behalf of My Son
movies.blurb: Anchored by a deeply affecting performance from Rejane Faria, Gabriel Martins’ moving drama follows a grieving mother seeking forgiveness from the families of a tragic bus accident. What unfolds is a profound meditation on guilt and whether forgiveness is possible.

movies.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
movies.blurb: Conceived in 1972 by legendary filmmaker William Greaves and completed 50 years later by his son David, Once Upon a Time in Harlem is an essential work of living archive, documenting a lively gathering of luminaries from the Harlem Renaissance during a cocktail party at Duke Ellington’s home.

movies.title: Onwards and Sideways
movies.blurb: The latest from Oscar-nominated director John Madden (Shakespeare in Love) stars Oscar nominee Laura Linney (TIFF ’08’s The Savages) and Rhys Ifans (TIFF ’23’s Mother Couch) as strangers whose lives become entwined when both are diagnosed with Parkinson disease.

movies.title: Our Loves
movies.blurb: The latest from Avi Nesher (TIFF '16's Past Life) is a gracefully woven drama about the ways that love intensifies and second chances are possible in the face of adversity and mayhem.

movies.title: Oxygen Masks Will (Not) Drop Automatically
movies.blurb: The first-ever series from renowned Brazilian filmmaker Marcelo Gomes tells the true story of a group of young flight attendants who smuggle treatment drugs from America into the hands of patients with AIDS in 1980s Brazil.

movies.title: Paradise Lost
movies.blurb: A bus full of children mysteriously vanishes. When an altered version of a grieving mother’s son returns years later, she must grapple with the technologically revised reality she has created in this sharp thriller from Yeon Sang-ho.

movies.title: Pelechian Project
movies.blurb:
North American premiere of 4K restorations!

 One of the year’s greatest cinematic gifts, this programme brings together five newly restored films by the pioneering Armenian filmmaker Artavazd Pelechian, each a harrowing ode to humanity, and its natural cycles of existence.

movies.title: Phoolan
movies.blurb: In the heartland of India, a young Phoolan Devi becomes one of the most famous outlaws in Indian history and the target of 2,000 heavily armed men sent to kill her over a gruelling 48-hour siege.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Possible Love
movies.blurb: Lee Chang-dong’s eagerly anticipated new film brings stories of relationships, generational and class divides, in this gripping tale of two couples playing games with themselves and one another.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Pretenders
movies.blurb: Tough, stylish, and effortlessly cool, the Pretenders founder Chrissie Hynde is the real thing. Grounded in extensive interviews with Hynde and archival materials, Pretenders chronicles the evolution of one of rock’s most singular icons.

movies.title: Prima Facie
movies.blurb: Oscar nominee Cynthia Erivo (Wicked) stars in this adaptation of Suzie Miller’s globally acclaimed play that examines what happens when an ambitious barrister who primarily defends those accused of sex crimes unexpectedly becomes the accuser in a sexual assault case.

movies.title: Purgatory
movies.blurb: This coming-of-age dramedy, set in the 1980s, follows Beatrice as she tries to reunite her recently separated parents, and stars J.K. Simmons, Abby Elliott, John Reynolds, and Jack Innanen.

movies.title: Rapinoe
movies.blurb: Soccer star Megan Rapinoe explores what it means to win and lose in this intimate portrait by Rebeca Huntt (Beba).

movies.title: Re/Pair
movies.blurb: Lacey Schwartz Delgado (Little White Lie) explores the bonds and tensions between American Black and Jewish communities in a series of dialogues with prominent figures.

movies.title: REDEFINED | Short Film Showcase
movies.blurb: Catch the premiere of REDEFINED at the Toronto International Film Festival and streaming worldwide on the NFB. Following the screening, join us for a Q&A with the filmmakers.

movies.title: Rehearsals for a Revolution
movies.blurb: Acclaimed actor-turned-documentarian Pegah Ahangarani draws on a trove of archival material to skillfully weave her personal narrative with Iranian politics over the past four decades.

movies.title: Report to Mother
movies.blurb:
North American Premiere of 4K restoration!

 A daring clarion call and one of the most significant works of Indian political cinema, John Abraham’s extraordinary final film Amma Ariyan (Report to Mother) follows a young man in 1970s Kerala as he journeys — with a progressive swell of companions — to inform a mother of her son’s death, amid widespread unrest.

movies.title: Rescue
movies.blurb: Director Sine Plambech (Heartbound, TIFF ’18) documents the kidnapping of a mother and her long quest to be reunited with her husband, illuminating a mass crisis experienced by migrants in the Mediterranean.

movies.title: River
movies.blurb: Joshua Giuliano makes an audacious debut with a suspenseful slasher that sets three embittered siblings adrift along a rural waterway, and in the sights of a masked killer.

movies.title: Rogue Trooper
movies.blurb: Directed by Duncan Jones (Moon, Warcraft), this outlandish animated adaptation of the influential British comic book follows a clone soldier bred for an interstellar forever-war and his fallen comrades whose personalities live on within his gun, helmet, and backpack.

movies.title: Run Terry Run
movies.blurb: This intimate and inspiring portrait from filmmaker Sean Menard (TIFF ’17’s The Carter Effect) draws upon never-before-seen footage to reveal the arduous process and profound commitment behind Terry Fox’s Marathon of Hope to raise awareness and money for cancer research.

movies.title: Salvation
movies.blurb: A hunger for purpose and a flair for delusion in a small Scottish town: Tom Nicoll’s debut is a sharp, empathetic portrait of young men adrift.

movies.title: Seventeen
movies.blurb: Three young queer Indigenous people’s lives intersect and overlap over the course of 17 hours in downtown Vancouver.

movies.title: Silenced Nights
movies.blurb: For some, staying silent is the only way to survive. Lawrence Fajardo’s bleak sociopolitical drama Silenced Nights follows a witness to an extrajudicial killing in a Philippines slum as he seeks to make the truth known.

movies.title: Sisters
movies.blurb: Outside of Madrid, two sisters unite their families on a summer weekend, celebrating milestones and the solstice-heralding San Juan Festival. However, joy quickly turns to horror when a serious allegation of sexual abuse surfaces from one of their children.

movies.title: Slow Horses
movies.blurb: The sixth season of this smash hit series finds the motley crew of disgraced MI5 agents in Slough House, working under the cantankerous Jackson Lamb (Gary Oldman, TIFF ’17’s Darkest Hour), thrown once again into the fray.

movies.title: Smudge the Blades
movies.blurb: A fresh take on the underdog sports film, centring on an Indigenous hockey team in Northern Alberta, from actor and director Cody Lightning (Hey, Viktor!, TIFF ’23) and starring Ed Helms, Jana Schmieding, and Paulina Alexis.

movies.title: Soumsoum, The Night of the Stars
movies.blurb: Five years after Lingui, the Sacred Bonds, Chadian director Mahamat-Saleh Haroun returns to TIFF with his latest feature, winner of the FIPRESCI Award at the 2026 Berlinale.

movies.title: Spirit Guardians: The Last Secret of the First Emperor
movies.blurb: The largest production in Vietnamese history, this sweeping epic from Nguyễn Phan Quang Binh (The Floating Lives) transports us to the Đinh dynasty, when a band of fearless warriors set out on a secret mission to safeguard a sacred mystery.

movies.title: Spring in a Small Town
movies.blurb:
World Premiere of 4K restoration! 

 Crowned the greatest Chinese film ever made by the Hong Kong Film Critics Society, director Fei Mu’s poetic, romantic 1948 masterpiece observes a bored wife enlivened by a surprise visit from an old flame, whose presence threatens to upend the matrimonial home.

movies.title: Still Night, Burning House
movies.blurb: A once-close family comes together to say goodbye to an uncle who struggled with mental health issues, in award-winning short filmmaker Carol Nguyen’s tender and emotional feature-length documentary debut.

movies.title: Strong Son
movies.blurb: A bodybuilder struggles to keep it together as he cares for his elderly father in this perceptive and deeply felt drama by Winnipeg’s Ian Bawa.

movies.title: Stuffed
movies.blurb: Love, death, and taxidermy collide in this gloriously twisted musical, one of the year’s funniest, most original, and unexpectedly heartfelt romances.

movies.title: Sunburn
movies.blurb: Over one hot summer day in Toronto, a group of young people try to survive the heatwave and a blackout by making jokes, roaming the city, and forming tangible connections that feel like they can disappear at any moment.

movies.title: Tangles
movies.blurb: A young woman deals with her vibrant mother’s Alzheimer diagnosis in this deeply moving animation adapted from a graphic memoir, with a voice cast including Abbi Jacobson, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Bryan Cranston, Seth Rogen, and Bowen Yang.

movies.title: Tehran, Under the Skin
movies.blurb: In an age of body anxiety, filmmaker Afsaneh Salari embeds herself in the offices of Iranian plastic surgeons to interview their clients with humour and empathy.

movies.title: Ten Dark Women
movies.blurb:
North American Premiere of 4K restoration!

 In the stylish, satirical, and ahead-of-its-time Ten Dark Women (Kuroi jûnin no onna, 1961), by legendary Japanese director Kon Ichikawa, 10 women discover they are sharing the same pathologically unfaithful man, and temporarily abandon jealousy to meticulously orchestrate a collective revenge.

movies.title: Tender Loving Care
movies.blurb: Seven-time Academy Award nominee Mike Leigh returns with an uplifting story of family and how to deal with grief, featuring remarkably emotional performances from Kate O’Flynn and Alice Bailey Johnson.

movies.title: Tenzing
movies.blurb: Starring Tom Hiddleston (TIFF ’24’s The Life of Chuck), Oscar nominee Willem Dafoe, and Genden Phuntsok (TIFF ’18’s Jinpa), this wondrous biopic recounts the story of Nepalese-Indian Sherpa mountaineer Tenzing Norgay who, alongside Edmund Hillary, became first to top Everest in 1953.

movies.title: The Age of Goodbyes
movies.blurb: Vivian Sung stars as the ravishing Du Li An in a breathtaking cinematic adaptation of Li Zi Shu’s The Age of Goodbyes, a story about memory, loss, love, doppelgängers, and hidden truths.

movies.title: The Assassin(s)
movies.blurb: Based on the attempted assassination of South Korean President Park Chung-hee, the latest from Hur Jin-ho (TIFF ’23’s A Normal Family) is a large-canvas procedural about police and journalists determined to uncover a seemingly impenetrable conspiracy.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Beloved
movies.blurb: Starring Oscar winner Javier Bardem and Victoria Luengo (TIFF ’24’s The Room Next Door), the latest from Rodrigo Sorogoyen (TIFF ’18’s The Realm) chronicles an unnerving collaboration between a charismatic, manipulative director and the actor daughter he hasn’t seen in 13 years.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Betrayers
movies.blurb: In adapting his own literary prize-winner, Toronto’s David Bezmozgis delivers a deft political thriller about the limits of love and loyalty.

movies.title: The Black Box is Orange
movies.blurb: The debut feature by Toronto artist and filmmaker Yuula Benivolski, The Black Box is Orange is a multimodal, autobiographical essay film that deploys both personal memory and incomplete archives to reflect on a childhood in a militarized border town.

movies.title: The bovine with the curved horns
movies.blurb: Blending Caribbean fantasy, magical realism, and Colombia’s painful history, The bovine with the curved horns follows a boy searching for his missing father through a landscape where myth and violence coexist. A haunting, poetic debut of remarkable beauty and emotional power.

movies.title: The City of the Living
movies.blurb: The City of the Living is Edoardo Gabbriellini’s (Holiday, TIFF ’23) gripping yet respectful anti-true crime film based on Nicola Lagioia’s bestselling literary chronicle about the senseless 2016 murder of a young man that rocked Rome.

movies.title: The Daughters of Abraham
movies.blurb: A young Muslim woman raised in Marseille reunites with a young Jewish woman after a period of estrangement, reconnecting as friends over summer break. When a sudden tragedy disrupts their carefree holiday, the pair face the similarities and differences that strengthen and threaten their relationship together.

movies.title: The Debut
movies.blurb: Jesse Eisenberg directs Academy Award winner Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti in a dark comedy about a bored suburban housewife who finds purpose acting in community theatre.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Diary of a Chambermaid
movies.blurb: Offering his most provocative work yet, the latest from Romanian provocateur Radu Jude is a surprisingly tender socioeconomic satire.

movies.title: The Difficult Bride
movies.blurb: Following the strange visions afflicting a woman on the cusp of marriage, the latest from Rubaiyat Hossain (TIFF ’19’s Made in Bangladesh) examines the pressures applied to brides in a milieu where weddings demand an asphyxiating feminine ideal.

movies.title: The Dreamed Adventure
movies.blurb: Winner of the Jury Prize in the competition section of the Cannes Film Festival, The Dreamed Adventure is German auteur Valeska Grisebach's highly anticipated and exceptional follow up to Western (TIFF ’17).

movies.title: The Face of Horror
movies.blurb: The Love Witch’s Anna Biller stunningly adapts the famous Japanese ghost story Yotsuya Kaidanto for 14th-century England in this gory tribute to classic Technicolor shockers.

movies.title: The Final Act
movies.blurb: Quebec’s Sophie Deraspe returns to the Festival with a philosophical and intimate look at the many profound issues surrounding both death and medically assisted dying in an extraordinary documentary.

movies.title: The Fortunate Isles
movies.blurb: In the 16th century, on the newly conquered Canary Islands, colonial misgivings intersect with personal desperation. Fátima, an enslaved and pregnant woman, must struggle to survive both the landscape, and the other inhabitants.

movies.title: The Housewife
movies.blurb: Grounded in artful performances from Oscar nominee Naomi Watts (TIFF ’01’s Mulholland Drive) and Tye Sheridan (TIFF ’13’s Joe), this salient historical drama depicts the complexities of seeking justice in the long shadow of Nazism.

movies.title: The Hummingbird Paints Fragrant Songs
movies.blurb: The Indigenous painter Sara Flores gets discovered by the international art world in her 70s, setting her off on an adventure as she travels from her home in the Peruvian Amazon to be fȇted in galleries from New York to Paris.

movies.title: The Idiot(s)
movies.blurb: Aimee Lou Wood and Johnny Flynn bring to life the story of Anna and Fyodor Dostoevsky, showcasing the troubled author and the woman who pushed him to write one of his greatest works.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Julia Set
movies.blurb: Chase Infiniti stars as a gifted university student who becomes romantically involved with a teaching assistant as they both prepare for the Putnam Exam, the most challenging math competition in North America. Gillian Anderson and Jason Isaacs co-star.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre
VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Liberation
movies.blurb: Carrie Coon soars in the riveting true story of filmmaker Guy Nattiv’s grandmother, whose humdrum day-to-day life is upended by a mysterious and entrancing young woman (Lily James) offering the promise of escape to something better.

movies.title: The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd
movies.blurb: Starring Oscar nominee Amanda Seyfried (The Testament of Ann Lee, TIFF ’25) and Scoot McNairy (Nightbitch, TIFF ’24), the latest from Tim Blake Nelson is a psychologically rich prison story about crime, punishment, and love.

movies.title: The Lost Children Of Tuam
movies.blurb: A quietly powerful true story of an amateur historian’s quest to uncover a long-buried injustice. By exposing what rightly became a national scandal, Catherine Corless changed Ireland forever.

movies.title: The Man I Love
movies.blurb: Ira Sachs’ vision of New York artists living under the spectre of AIDS in the ’80s focuses on the joy and salvation of creativity.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
movies.blurb: Anchored by John Turturro’s charismatic performance, this low-key crime drama from Noah Segan (Blood Relatives) harkens back to the character-driven films of 1970s New Hollywood.

movies.title: The Pervert's Guide to Utopias
movies.blurb: Twenty years after The Pervert’s Guide to Cinema, the renowned intellectual Slavoj Žižek reunites with director Sophie Fiennes for a fresh meditation on movies and ideas that crackles with energy.

movies.title: The Remotes
movies.blurb: This ambitious, beguiling narrative debut from acclaimed Filipino filmmaker and experimentalist John Torres follows a grieving detective who finds himself increasingly ensnared while investigating a case involving a sinister navigation app causing physical and psychological debris.

movies.title: The Road Not Taken
movies.blurb: Peter Ho-Sun Chan directs Zhou Xun, Wen Qi, Tian Zhuangzhuang and Wang Xiao in a drama about early-onset Alzheimer disease. Combining expert storytelling with commercial appeal, The Road Not Taken reflects on what remains when our understanding of the world begins to disappear.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: The Secret Lives of Baba Segi's Wives
movies.blurb: A wealthy patriarch’s fragile household unravels when the youngest of his four wives fails to conceive. Blending sharp Nollywood wit with tenderness, this deeply satisfying drama explores topics of infertility, gendered inheritance, and shifting family power.

movies.title: The Smell of Apples
movies.blurb: In John Trengove’s relentless third feature, a sheltered 11-year-old white South African boy gradually comes to realize the horrors of the apartheid system.

movies.title: The Spiral
movies.blurb: Director Paolo Strippoli turns the screws on a desperate mother (Jasmine Trinca) as she confesses a series of Faustian bargains to her estranged daughter (Romana Maggiora Vergano) in this riveting morality chiller.

movies.title: The Stunt Driver
movies.blurb: Jay Baruchel and director Michael Dowse re-team for a raucous yet heartfelt comedy about a Canadian stuntman who dared to dream big and fly (very) high.

movies.title: The Surgeon
movies.blurb: Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh (Everything Everywhere All at Once) is back in action as a kidnapped surgeon forced to perform one last operation in this fun, pulse-pounding thriller.

movies.title: The Ultra Runner
movies.blurb: Punishing tests of human endurance become a means of escaping past demons for the unforgettable subject of Mila Aung-Thwin’s superb new film.

movies.title: The Unknown
movies.blurb: A highlight of this year’s Cannes Competition, the third feature by acclaimed French filmmaker, actor, and screenwriter Arthur Harari (co-writer of Anatomy of a Fall) is a moody, existential body-swap puzzler starring an extraordinary Léa Seydoux and a near-unrecognizable Niels Schneider.

movies.title: The Violinist
movies.blurb: Winner of this year’s Annecy Cristal award, this intimate animation about two violinists in Singapore circa WWII highlights the healing power of music while pulling heartstrings.

movies.title: The World Before
movies.blurb: Yoon Dan-bi’s coming-of-age story follows two childhood best friends who reunite for a summer on a remote Korean island. This beautifully constructed slice of life captures the emotional intensity of adolescence through assured filmmaking and compelling performances.

movies.title: Thirteen in Gaza
movies.blurb: Palestinian director Hosam Abu Dan makes his narrative feature debut with a nuanced and deeply human portrait of a father and his teenage daughter navigating everyday life in a refugee camp in the Gaza Strip.

movies.title: Toy Gun Bandit
movies.blurb: A prank gone wrong launches a Quebec teen into a life of crime in Rémi St-Michel’s energetic and unpredictable second feature.

movies.title: Trash Mountain
movies.blurb: After the death of their hoarder father in rural Missouri, two siblings (Caleb Hearon and Zooey Deschanel) reunite to sort through the baggage — both literal and emotional — in Kris Rey’s poignant and funny exploration of love and grief.

movies.title: Trees are Watching
movies.blurb: Iranian Kurdish auteur Bahman Ghobadi blends psychological horror and ecological allegory as he depicts the eerie haunting of a writer (Eva Green) reckoning with past misdeeds under the ominous gaze of a pair of trees and a malignant wooden chair.

movies.title: Turtle Island Rap
movies.blurb: The bumpy road to success experienced by three aspiring Indigenous hip-hop artists is the focus of Alexandra Lazarowich’s (Fast Horse) verité-style feature documentary debut.

movies.title: Union Town
movies.blurb: Barbara Kopple (TIFF ’76’s Harlan County, U.S.A.) looks at three crucial labour battles as they unfold in New York City involving workers from UPS, Amazon, and deliveristas for DoorDash and GrubHub.

movies.title: Up Against It
movies.blurb: Post-marital acrimony and parental devotion make strange bedfellows in Trudie Styler’s wicked comedy, starring Oscar nominee Antonio Banderas (TIFF ’19’s Pain and Glory) and Eva Birthistle (TIFF ’05’s Imagine Me & You) as co-parenting divorcees faced with an indecent proposal.

movies.title: Villeneuve: The Rise of a Legend
movies.blurb: Chronicling the exhilarating career of Gilles Villeneuve, one of Canada’s foremost athletes, this biopic from director Yan Lanouette Turgeon stars Rémi Goulet as the kid from Quebec who changed Formula One.

screenings.venue: VISA Screening Room at the Princess of Wales Theatre

movies.title: Vintage Violence
movies.blurb: In Eugene Kotlyarenko’s mixed-media caper, a livestreamer (Cole Sprouse) discovers a cache of vintage denim only to run afoul of the Yakuza when he is lured to Japan to sell the jeans by one of his subscribers (Kiko Mizuhara).

movies.title: Viva Carmen
movies.blurb: A vibrant reframing of Bizet’s famous opera through the lens of a pack of Sevillian street children who are determined to subvert Carmen’s tragic fate. With an intimate approach to music and bold brushstrokes that dance, this animated feature sings brightly.

movies.title: Voices
movies.blurb: A starry-eyed bellhop (Francis Edemobi) enlists his friends to help him exploit an unsavoury opportunity that could secure them fame and fortune in Deantè Gray’s soulful, suspenseful 1960s-set musical chamber thriller.

movies.title: Wavelengths 1: House and Home
movies.blurb: Bringing together new work by John Smith, Rita Ferrando, Jiaqi Yu, Danaya Chulphuthiphong, Mustafa Uzuner, and Natalia Marín, the films in this programme reflect on the nature of abodes, both fixed and temporary, and the limit of refuge.

movies.title: Wavelengths 2: This Suffocating Now
movies.blurb: Featuring new films by Maryam Tafakory, Zheng Lu Xinyuan, Simon Liu, and Vika Kirchenbauer, alongside a rediscovered and restored short by Takehisa Kosugi, the films in this programme speak to the political potential of creative work, creative scenes, and companionship.

movies.title: Wavelengths 3: Time and Tide
movies.blurb: Featuring new work by James Richards and Ben Russell, a rare 70mm projection by Johann Lurf, and a tribute to the recently departed Yervant Gianikian, the films of Time and Tide bend eras, epochs, and the cosmos with both verve and grace.

movies.title: Wavelengths: Anoushahpour/Aljafari
movies.blurb: Bringing together new works by Parastoo Anoushahpour and Kamal Aljafari, the two films in this programme reflect on the meeting point between imagination and memory — both personal and collective — from the perspective of children and the aged.

movies.title: We Are All Strangers
movies.blurb: Anthony Chen, a Festival favourite and the helmer behind Ilo Ilo, reunites with muses Yeo Yann Yann and Koh Jia Ler in an emotionally charged drama about a constructed family to close his “Growing Up” trilogy.

movies.title: We Are Born Good
movies.blurb: Golden Horse winner Suet Ying Chung and Wai Lun Yeung lead Leung Chuen Yeung’s assured debut, in which a struggling actress and an ex-con restaurant owner turn a petty dispute into an unlikely bond. Witty, moving, and accessible.

movies.title: What Lies Between Us
movies.blurb: From Danish director Amalie Næsby Fick and a cast led by Sidse Babett Knudsen comes a compelling cautionary tale about the ethical and moral boundaries a parent may cross in order to protect a child.

movies.title: Whatcha Want
movies.blurb: The latest comedy from writer-director Mina Shum (Double Happiness, TIFF ’17’s Meditation Park) tells the story of a young woman from Hong Kong whose marriage to an affluent businessman is beginning to resemble a gilded cage.

movies.title: Where the River Begins
movies.blurb: In Juan Andrés Arango’s bracing and poetic third feature, an Emberá woman displaced by violence undertakes a dangerous journey to find a better life for herself and her daughter.

movies.title: Wild Horse Nine
movies.blurb: Two CIA agents (John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell) are sent on a mission to Easter Island, where one faces an existential crisis over his past actions, in Martin McDonagh’s latest dark comedy.

movies.title: Wild Wild East
movies.blurb: Set in occupied Poland in the middle of the Second World War, Jan Holoubek’s tour-de-force is part suspenseful western, part gritty wartime noir.

movies.title: Woman Unknown
movies.blurb: A woman with secrets to hide desperately tries to avoid mob justice in postwar Copenhagen in May el-Toukhy’s bracing third feature.

movies.title: YAGA
movies.blurb: Starring Canadians Hudson Williams, Noah Reid, and Carrie-Anne Moss, this adaptation of Kat Sandler’s award-winning play unfurls the truth behind a mysterious disappearance in a small coastal town.

movies.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
movies.blurb: Oscar winner Mahershala Ali (TIFF ’18 People’s Choice Award winner Green Book) stars as a devout Muslim, loving family man, and contract killer in this audaciously inventive Texas-set action thriller from writer-director Bassam Tariq (Mogul Mowgli).

movies.title: Zjili: A Story of Sisterhood and The Burdens of Excess
movies.blurb: In their poignant debut feature, co-directors Christine Boateng and Hajara Musah Chambas depict the journey of three Ghanaian women eking out a living as kayayei or porters in the trenches of the world’s largest secondhand clothing market.
